children: By Neil Mehta, Dana Mattioli and Caitlin Ostroff
The investment fund 1789 Capital, in which Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, is investing around $300 million into Polymarket, according to a person familiar with the matter.
The investment is part of a $1 billion round led by 1789 that would value Polymarket at $21 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

The investment will make 1789 one of Polymarket's largest backers. Intercontinental Exchange, Polymarket's largest investor, disclosed in July that its $1.6 billion stake in Polymarket amounted to 22% of the company's shares outstanding.

Polymarket, along with rival Kalshi, has attracted controversy for permitting users to place bets on sports, which some regulators have criticized as gambling. Both platforms have listed markets that have led to charges of insider trading. Both also see more traders losing money than winning, The Journal previously reported.
1789 had previously invested a total of around $200 million into Polymarket, according to a person familiar with the investments.
Polymarket has a data partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of The Wall Street Journal. Bloomberg previously reported that 1789 was leading the billion-dollar round.

1789 made its first investment in Polymarket before the 2024 election. That year, Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan was seen at a table with Trump Jr. and Omeed Malik, founder of 1789 Capital, at the Republican National Convention.
After his father won the presidential election, Donald Trump Jr. joined 1789 as a partner and the firm invested in Polymarket again.

Earlier in August, Malik hosted a Republican fundraiser with Vice President JD Vance at Malik's New York Hamptons home. Among the attendees were Trump Jr. and Polymarket's chief executive, Shayne Coplan.

The venture-capital firm's success has attracted scrutiny from House Democrats. Last week, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D., Md.) wrote to 1789's leadership demanding a list of the firm's investments, communications with the government and information about its decision to hire Trump Jr.
1789's counsel denied any allegations of conflicts of interest as "unsubstantiated talking points."
Through the third quarter, 1789 has had 200% returns in its growth equity fund, the fund that the Polymarket investment is through, according to a person familiar with the matter.

In March, Trump Jr. spoke about the benefits of prediction markets during headline remarks at a conference of the Republican Attorneys General Association, and urged attendees to leave regulation to the federal government, according to people present. The remarks were first reported by the New York Times.
State attorneys general almost unanimously support state, not federal, regulation of the platforms, and more than a dozen states are fighting prediction markets over the issue in courts.
